topIssues.title: op-supernode: SuperRoots for the unsafe
topIssues.author: Inphi
topIssues.body:
Currently, fetching super roots from supernode via atTimestamp fails if no verified or safe data exists at the referenced timestamp. It may be useful for supernode to return super roots in this case anyway.

I'm not fully convinced this is needed, but logging it here in case it proves useful later. It may make more sense to introduce a different RPC that provides possibly unverified super roots, so as to not complicate the atTimestamp RPC response.

topIssues.title: op-supernode: HTTP L1 URLs result in disabled polling, virtual nodes never receive L1 head updates
topIssues.author: Inphi
topIssues.body:
When op-supernode is configured with an HTTP L1 RPC URL (though not a websocket URL), the L1 polling mechanism is inadvertently disabled, causing virtual nodes to never receive L1 head updates via subscription. This results in stale L1 views for all managed chains.

As a result of this:
- Virtual nodes within op-supernode will have stale L1 chain views
- L1 head subscriptions will never fire when using HTTP URLs
- Safe/finalized block tracking via `eth.PollBlockChanges` still works (separate mechanism), but `newHeads` subscriptions are broken

This affects derivation and any L1 head-dependent logic in the inner op-nodes

topIssues.title: op-supernode: Reset Handling
topIssues.author: axelKingsley
topIssues.body:
# Context

Supernode exists to drive complex or extended protocols through derivation and verification. For example, Supernode's Interop Activity confirms that the chains being derived all contain valid Executing Messages.

Because Verification occurs based on chain state, it is *REQUIRED* that the EVM underneath the Supernode sometimes arrive at chain states which are invalid. Invalid Executing Messages must exist to be deemed invalid.

AND YET! The Supernode must allow follow the canonical chain in order to *continue* verifying blocks.

Fundamentally, this means we need the ability to *rewind*, *truncate*, *reorg* or *reset* the Chain State which the Supernode uses.

# Reset Requirements

Resets should follow timestamp as their primary indexing, and should be chain specific.

`Supernode.Reset(ChainID, Timestamp)`

Likely, this functionality only needs to be fully exposed at the Chain Container Level, for production/interop purposes

`ChainContainer.Reset(Timestamp)`

When Resetting, the Chain Container is responsible for fully restoring the chain state to the expected timestamp. This means it should:
- Suspend the ongoing Virutal Node
- Reset the Executing Engine to truncate data beyond the timestamp
- Resume the ongoing Virtual Node

This is the strategy employed in the SV2 spike, logic flow available here: https://www.notion.so/oplabs/Supervisor-V2-Main-Loop-and-Logic-Flow-Diagrams-265f153ee162804388dac933f525de7b

# Considerations
- In the POC, we had to use `DebugSetHead`. Hopefully we can find a cleaner way to handle it
- It might be prudent to manually truncate the SafeDB while the CL is being replaced since we have a handle to it, but the CL should also handle that.

# Tools at your disposal
- The Chain Container loop already is pretty graceful about replacing the Virtual Node. A new VN is created with a new `vn_id` and all prior resources are hooked to it.
- Engine Controller as an entity can house all the complexity for resetting the EL. The Chain Container keeps a persistent handle over the EVM across all VNs so it can do work like this and also read state.

# How it connects to other work
- When Interop Activity discovers a bad block it's going to tell the Chain Container via a `InvalidateBlock` function
- Invalidate block will cause the Chain Container to store the ID in the "Denylist" registry, which prevents re-derivation to invalid blocks
- The chain container will *then also* notice the EVM is on that invalid state, and will trigger a reset

# How you can test this work
- Gotta get Acceptance Testing built out more, but there's already a preset for the Supernode we can build from
- You could easily build a reset API by implementing an `RPCActivity` that triggers the functionality. That way you could run the supernode locally and poke the feature. You wouldn't need to commit the activity since there's no production reason to reset nodes (though... maybe that's the start of an admin API)

# Definition of Done

- A Chain can be reset back to a timestamp
- Without further integration to Verification Activities, the same chain-state is expected to re-derive
- We should be able to see this live through some demo
- Unit tests from the Chain Container that the correct calls to the CL+EL are being done and VN is replaced
- Integration (Acceptance) test that demonstrates reset and re-derivation

topPRs.title: op-devstack: add sysgo integration for op-interop-filter
topPRs.author: opsuperchain
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds sysgo test infrastructure for the op-interop-filter service, following the established patterns from supervisor and batcher.

**New files:**
- `stack/interop_filter.go`: ID type and interface definitions
- `shim/interop_filter.go`: RPC client wrapper for tests
- `sysgo/interop_filter.go`: Service wrapper with `WithInteropFilter` option
- `sysgo/interop_filter_test.go`: Basic integration tests

**Modified files:**
- `filter/service.go`: Added `HTTPEndpoint()` method
- `stack/system.go`: Added InteropFilter methods to System interface
- `shim/system.go`: Added interop filter storage and accessors
- `sysgo/orchestrator.go`: Added interopFilters registry and hydration
- `stack/matcher.go`: Added InteropFilterMatcher type
- `stack/match/first.go`: Added FirstInteropFilter matcher

## Design Notes

- **ControlPlane integration not added**: The interop filter is similar to auxiliary services like batcher/proposer rather than core infrastructure nodes (supervisor, L2CL, L2EL). ControlPlane integration can be added if needed for test scenarios requiring programmatic stop/start of the filter.

- **TCP proxy pattern**: Uses the same proxy pattern as supervisor for stable RPC endpoints during test setup.

- **RPC namespace**: Uses `supervisor_checkAccessList` intentionally for API compatibility with the supervisor.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./op-devstack/...` passes
- [x] `go build ./op-interop-filter/...` passes
- [ ] `go test ./op-devstack/sysgo/... -run TestInteropFilter` (requires contracts build)

topPRs.title: op-supernode: SuperAuthority Object
topPRs.author: axelKingsley
topPRs.body:
An empty object, meant to be extended with function-attributes, from which the Virtual `op-node` can make requests of the containing Supernode.

The Supernode object is currently empty so that it can be extended easily without future merge conflicts. I anticipate it will serve:
- isBlockVerified - can identify if verifiers have fully verified the given block
- isBlockInvalid - matches for already known invalid blocks so the payload isn't applied again

This object is like an Interface+Client for the supernode itself, but special purpose for the virtual nodes it contains. When a node sees that its SuperAuthority object is not nil, it can use the functions as authoritative signals, even if it does not understand those signals. Since it is an Authority and it is concerned with Superlayer concerns, I figure SuperAuthority is the right name. But happy to change it.

topPRs.title: op-supernode: Interop Message Validation
topPRs.author: axelKingsley
topPRs.body:
# Note
The current state of this code is:
- Generation: Entirely Generated/Directed with Opus 4.5
- Review: Yet unreviewed by the author, oversight into tricky parts
- Tests: The model was directed to complete this work in a TDD way, so tests were built first, then implementation to satisfy it.

# What
Implements the actual Message Validation task of Interop. _Does Not_ yet have any handling for the invalid blocks it discovers.
Invalid messages in blocks cause a chain halt, which is demonstrated by an acceptance test.

# How

### 1. Acceptance Test (op-acceptance-tests)
- New: TestSupernodeInteropInvalidMessageHalt - An end-to-end test that sends a valid initiating message, then an invalid executing message (with bogus LogIndex=9999), and verifies that interop validity halts at the invalid block while safe/unsafe heads continue advancing on the Virtual Nodes.

### 2. LogsDB Infrastructure (logdb.go)
- New: Per-chain logs.DB instances managed by the interop activity for persisting L2 logs.
- LogsDB interface abstracting the database operations
- loadLogs - fetches receipts from each chain and stores logs at each timestamp
- processBlockLogs - extracts logs from receipts, identifies executing messages, and seals blocks
- verifyPreviousTimestampSealed - ensures sequential timestamp processing with chain continuity checks

### 3. Verification Logic (algo.go)
- New: Core algorithm for validating cross-chain messages.
verifyInteropMessages - for each chain, opens the block from logsDB and validates all executing messages
- verifyExecutingMessage - checks that the referenced initiating message exists in the source chain's logsDB and that timestamp ordering is correct (initiating < executing)

### 4. Chain Container / Engine Controller
- New: FetchReceipts(ctx, blockID) method added to:
  - ChainContainer interface
  - EngineController interface
  - l2Provider interface
  - This provides the interop activity access to transaction receipts needed for log extraction.

### 5. Result Types (types.go)
- Result struct InvalidHeads map is populated with any blocks which are not valid during validation.
